text: Now watch three different molecules try the active site. This one drifts in and does not fit; it slides off. This one, the same. This one settles in, cleanly. The active site is complementary in shape to this substrate: not the same shape, complementary. That is enzyme specificity: an enzyme acts on a particular substrate or a limited group of related substrates. These two molecules do not fit this active site. Picture a lock and a key; and written properly: the active site is complementary in shape to its substrate, so the enzyme is specific.
